units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 2:10:4">Y. B. Mets. II, end, 8ᵈ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 23:4">Ex. XXIII, 4</cite>) <he>יכול פ׳ ממש</he> you might think, it means literally ‘striking against’ (and not merely seeing); Bab.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 33a:5">Ib.</cite> <he>ואיזו היא ראייה שיש בה פ׳</he> and what is a ‘seeing’ which may be called ‘meeting’?; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 352:7">Yalk. Ex. 352</cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 8:4">B. Kam. VIII, 4</cite> <he>העבד … פְּגִיעָתָן רעה וכ׳</he> coming in (hostile) contact with a slave or a woman is bad, for he who injures them is made responsible, whereas if they injure you, they cannot be made responsible (having no property of their own).
Y. Ber. IV, 7ᵇ top (ref. to ויפגע, Gen. XXVIII, 11) אין פ׳ אלא תפלה the expression pagʿa means prayer (with ref. to Jer. XXVII, 18; VII, 16); Gen. R. s. 68; Sot. 14ᵃ; a. fr.
